newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia cuts VAT from 20.0 to 17.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Zambia cuts VAT from 20.0 to 17.5 percent.

text.p: The Zambian government said on Monday it would cut Value Added Tax (VAT) by 2.5 percentage points to 17.5 percent on Monday night.
"Value Added Tax will be cut from 20 percent to 17.5 percent effctive from midnight tonight," a spokesman said.

Finance Minister Ronald Penza said in January that VAT would be cut during the year to stimulate private sector-led economic growth, although analysts had expected tax increases in 1997 to make up for cuts in western donor aid.

Penza said last week that he expected donors to restore normal aid flows -- which were cut following concerns about the conduct of last year's elections -- at a Consultative Group meeting set for July 9.
"We are doing everything we agreed with our cooperating patterns. Assuming that everything remains in order, we are confident of a positive outcome of the Consultative Group meeting," Penza said.
